Outline: Caelen observes the masked man in purple dismissing the violence he just enacted as irrelevant noise. The guard leaves Caelen broken on the floor, reinforcing that brute force is not the currency of this place. Caelen shifts from panic-induced reaction to cold, tactical observation. He notes the ledger being written upon—the primary tool of power here. Realizing his physical strength and combat instincts are currently liabilities due to his injuries and language barrier, he begins to formulate a new strategy: he must become an asset in their eyes to survive. Prose:
The threat of the staff vanished as quickly as it had arrived, leaving Caelen with nothing but the cold weight of his own broken body against the stone floor. The guard had withdrawn, wiping dust from his hands as if discarding a minor inconvenience, then turned away without another word of warning or explanation. Caelen lay pinned beneath the heavy gravity that made every breath a labor and every movement a negotiation with pain. He tried to push himself up, but his ribs screamed in protest, forcing him to lie still again.

He watched the masked man in purple step forward from his ledger-bound post, cane tapping a slow, rhythmic beat against the stone floor. The man did not intervene to stop the violence; he watched with detached curiosity, his pale eyes scanning Caelen’s fallen posture like one might examine a discarded insect. The staff-bearing guard straightened, then turned away without another word of warning or explanation, leaving Caelen pinned beneath the weight of the moment.

The man in purple flipped another page of his ledger, indifferent to the disruption. He spoke again, his voice carrying a flat, procedural tone that Caelen could not translate, dismissing the guard and the broken scene alike. Caelen remained on his side, body anchored by unfamiliar gravity, chest heaving as pain bloomed across his shattered ribs. He had tried to save someone, and now he was broken again, a liability in eyes that saw only weakness.

He watched the man in purple’s hands move over the ledger, flipping pages with deliberate care. The black-tipped cane tapped rhythmically, conducting some unseen orchestra of humiliation. Caelen realized then that violence alone yielded no reward here; survival required becoming an asset before a liability. He accepted his broken ribs as a permanent condition for now, focusing entirely on the masked man’s ledger to understand what value he might offer or hide.

The harsh consonants and rolling vowels of the masked man's speech washed over him, unintelligible but carrying weight. The man seemed to be assessing them all, perhaps cataloging their worth in some way that Caelen could not yet decipher. There was no malice in the man's indifference, only a cold efficiency that chilled Caelen more than any blade ever had. He understood now that his instincts for combat were useless here; he needed to learn how to manipulate perception rather than just endure pain.

Caelen shifted slightly, testing the range of motion allowed by his cord bindings. The friction left raw, stinging trails on his skin, but he ignored the pain. His mind began to work in a new way, calculating where he could fit into this system without being discarded. He was no longer just a Marine who had failed; he was something else entirely, something that needed to be useful to survive. The man in purple's indifference confirmed it: in this closed system, his only leverage was perceived utility to the captors.
